text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Electronics UN49KS8000 49-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2016 Model) I was hesitant to buy a TV online but went to several local stores and many were out of stock since they were transitioning to 2017 models. So I decided to try Amazon on this 2016 Samsung that had many good reviews and was a good price. I was very impressed with both the TV and the delivery from Amazon.
Delivery: I was able to select which day I wanted it delivered and then was kept updated on the delivery status by Amazon. The delivery company called a few days in advance to verify a 3 hour window of time, and they did arrive that day within the window of time even though it was 10 min prior to the end of that time. They brought the TV in, removed it from the boxing, placed it on our TV stand, plugged it in and verified it was functioning. They took a picture of the functioning TV and took the old box/trash away. I was very pleased with the delivery.
The TV: It is great! Have only used the TV for four days but it has been used a lot during that timeframe. We replaced an older Samsung flatscreen (HD TV) with this one and wow, what a difference. Out of the box without any tuning whatsoever this is a great looking deep colored screen. With a few tweaks it is amazing. There were easy step-by-step onscreen setup instructions. The remote is lot better than the older large clunky devices and is a smart remote that even recognizes voice commands. I liked the concept of having just one cable to the TV which then links to a hub where you plug in other devices. Only issue I had was the TV remote could not recognize my Tivo device from my cable provider for all functions, but it did change channels and volume. I use a generic remote anyway which worked great with the new TV. The bezel is very small and the thickness of the TV is perfect for us.
Overall I was impressed with this TV and would highly recommend it, especially at the discounted price. I’ve already seen reviews of the 2017 version of this TV and some are not very favorable so I'm glad I bought this one.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Electronics UN49KS8000 49-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2016 Model)

Technology has advanced during those years, though, and this device is a bit more sophisticated in some ways than my old Bluetooth.

Just like my old Bluetooth, this one claims to have 11 hours of battery life when fully charged, and just like my old Bluetooth, its charge doesn’t last nearly that long. However, this model fully rechargs fairly rapidly, in under an hour, much faster than my old Bluetooth.

If I have this particular style of Bluetooth in my ear more than an hour, my ear gets sore. But the good news is that the ear hook allows it to stay firmly in place, even if bending over or exercising.

This Bluetooth pairs easily. I haven’t tried to pair it simultaneously with more than one phone, though the manufacturer claims it has that capability.

The sound quality is good not only for listening to calls and being heard clearly on the other end of a call, it is also good enough to listen to podcasts, audiobooks or music. However, other than for receiving or making calls, I much prefer other styles of Bluetooth to this one for listening to entertainment media, because I can keep their ear pieces in my ears for hours without discomfort, unlike this type of design.

Roku 2 XS 1080p Streaming Player (Old Model) I've been thinking about getting a Roku for some time, so when it was a Gold Box deal I took the plunge. I'm now kicking myself for not buying it sooner - this is great! Rather than be limited to streaming on my laptop, I can now stream from Amazon Prime and Netflix on the TV, plus have the sound routed through my home theater setup.

Setup of the Roku was about as simple as could be. I was up and running in less than 30 minutes, with a large portion of that time spent downloading updates or figuring out how to route the cables so they would not appear as attractive playthings for the cats. I hardwired this into my router rather than go wireless since the router is just a few feet away from the player.

I hooked the HDMI cable into my home theater receiver. I really can't tell the difference between streaming and playing a Blu-ray or DVD in terms of sound or video quality. My internet connection is 30Mbps.

I was surprised at how small the box is. Just a few inches wide and about an inch or so thick. I think the HDMI cable weighs more than the actual device. Very easy to find a spot to put it.

The remote is OK. I wish the buttons were a bit larger and/or were backlit so you can see them in a darkened room. It's usable and functional, but pretty basic.

Highly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Roku 2 XS 1080p Streaming Player (Old Model)

Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US) Though I am giving a review for this backpack, I can't come from the perspective of having used it for a while. I only received my Targus backpack yesterday, but from the looks of it I am pretty darn sure this backpack will last a long, long time. I've used MANY backpacks in the past carrying books, laptops and supplies during the time it took to earn two separate college degrees, and at my previous job of 17 years. I had to carry tools, manuals, laptops and assorted parts to calibrate monitoring equipment around my state. I was rough on the backpacks and some wore out.

I really wish I had had a backpack like this one. It's very well constructed out of strong materials, has a plethora of pockets and places to organize your stuff, and though I don't have a 17" notebook as of yet, it appears to be deep and wide and should easily fit one. There are even slots for file folders and inside zipper pouches. There are pockets on the inside and pockets on the outside. The bottom inside has a foam rubber "shock pad" that neatly folds down flat on the bottom of the backpack and is about 1/2" thick. Plus the bottom is covered in a waterproof rubbery material that should definitely help keep water from seeping up into the bag. That happened to me several times on my job with my other backpacks and it was really frustrating. It's very easy to set your backpack down on the ground not realizing the area is wet.

The shoulder straps are padded and adjustable, and it has a waist strap for extra stability. Even if you didn't use this backpack to tote your 17" marvel of technology around, it would serve well as a camper/hiker backpack. I can't wait to start using it. If something should go wrong or tear up, I will most definitely update this review telling about it, but for now I can find no fault whatsoever with it.
text_fidelity_b: Targus Demolition Backpack Designed to Fit up to 17.3-Inch Laptop, Black (TSB220US)

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Express - HD Streaming Player It may not be a techie's delight, but if you are looking for a budget streaming device, this one fits the bill. First off it is quite small making it ideal for cramped or limited spaces like a vacation home or boat. It comes with a short, two foot long cable and a piece of two sided tape. It connects to your tv with the cable.Depending where you tv is located you might have to use a longer cable. I did and found that the tape is not just a nice idea, it is a necessity. the box is so small and most cables so rigid it flips the box off making it impossible to regulate with the infrared remote. Take time to position because while the tape adheres well it looses its stickiness after being removed and repositioned. The infrared remote must be in line of sight for it to work. The way around that is to use the app. The app works with both android and iOS. The app has a voice control which I found to be inconsistent and a private listening feature that lets you use your phone headphones and mute the TV.

Performance is mixed. navigating and launching is slow. Netflix in particular really dragged. but playing content was excellent with no lag or problems. the channel selection is good with pretty much everything you would want available.

This is not bad for a budget streamer. there are definitely downsides, the ir remote, the lack of speed, the need for a cable. but it does work and is small enough for travel. I am frequently on the road for business and this does expand the limited options of hotel televisions. If you are on a budget and don't need or want the features that are available on pricier models this low end streamer will get the job done.
text_fidelity_b: Roku Express - HD Streaming Player

There's really only one main negative, and it's a big one. This cover has no way to attach the folded back front cover while reading. It folds back, and it can be held back by hand, but there's no catch or strap to keep it folded back. For a kindle, that's huge. I would not purchase a case without such a feature. This is especially the case with the voyage, which is meant to be a heavy reader's kindle.

I also tried sticking my kindle 4 into this case, and it fit pretty well. If you were caught in a pinch with no case, you could definitely use this for a regular kindle too.

HP Sprocket Portable Color Photo Printer, Print Social Media Photos on 2x3" Sticky-Backed Paper - Black (X7N08A) This is a great improvement over an earlier-gen ZINK paper ("zero ink") portable printer we have, which requires a wired connection and a proprietary charger, and no longer holds a charge well.

The HP Sprocket connects and prints wirelessly, charges from a standard micro-USB cable, and has a lithium-ion battery which is sure to last a lot longer.

We had it unboxed and printing in less than 5 minutes. You run it from a free app available for Android or Apple iOS devices. We used the Android version and it works great.

It takes less than 30 seconds to wirelessly send and print a photo. The prints are 2 inches by 3 inches, smooth and glossy, good resolution, and have a peel-and-stick backing for quick and easy mounting. In the long run, the priciest thing about a ZINK printer is the paper, so shop around for deals.

The prints came out a little to the warm side in color when sent "as is," but the app allows a lot of enhancement and has lots of effects you can add.

The Sprocket printer itself measures only 3 inches by 5 inches and less than an inch thick, and weighs about 6-and-a-half ounces. It's very portable.

And it's loads of fun.
text_fidelity_b: HP Sprocket Portable Color Photo Printer, Print Social Media Photos on 2x3" Sticky-Backed Paper - Black (X7N08A)

MavisLink HDMI Cable Fiber Optic 100ft 4K 60Hz HDMI2.0b 18Gbps HDR10 ARC HDCP2.2 YUV4:4:4/4:2:2/4:2:0 Slim Flexible for HDTV/Game Console/Projector/Home Theatre I gave this a four because it did not work on one out of three devices I tried it with (and I know each to work with a short HDMI cable). I'm not sure why this had a lot of flickering when used with my Alienware computer, but it worked perfectly with another computer and my QNAP NAS (worth noting is the NAS puts out a very weak signal and does not work with my in-place 25-ft. traditional HDMI cable).

I had almost written this off because usually HDMI is a crapshoot when it comes to any sort of distance and I didn't even realize such a product existed until I read about fiber optic cable inside. I thought that was a generic brand typo type of situation until I looked this up and realized this is a real thing. I didn't study it, but I gather/assume that there is a chip inside that changes electrical signals to low power lasers to send the signals this way. Interesting, though, because there are not 19 fibers inside (a traditional HDMI cable has 19 pins, I think).

I probably need to research this further just because it's totally cool, but I love this thing because I can now watch my NAS directly on my TV even though it is down in the basement (and there is a great app to act as a remote since I now do not have line of sight for the IR remote). I only took off a star because it apparently has some issues with my one computer - not sure why but if you need a couple of these, you might want to buy one at a time to be sure what it does and does not work with. I love it, but had to remove a star for that reason.
text_fidelity_b: MavisLink HDMI Cable Fiber Optic 100ft 4K 60Hz HDMI2.0b 18Gbps HDR10 ARC HDCP2.2 YUV4:4:4/4:2:2/4:2:0 Slim Flexible for HDTV/Game Console/Projector/Home Theatre

HAOHUNT Camcorder Digital Video Camera HD 1080P 30fps 3.0 INCH Touch Screen 24MP Camcorder with Microphone and Wide Angle Lens Vlogging Camera with Remote Control Infrared Night Vision Recorder I am impressed right off the bat with just how many useful accessories are included right off the bat. The description says it does not come with an SD card or AAA batteries, but mine did, perhaps for review purposes, although the box did not look like it had been opened. Seems like it would come with that stuff, so perhaps other reviewers might clarify. There is a case and two separate pouches for the wider camera lens and the microphone.

Functionality and video quality are pretty good. I guess the only drawback is that this almost seems like a throwback now. For still pictures - on a vacation or a great hike where I want to take great pictures - I still take along a small camera instead of just my cell phone, but the truth is cell phone cameras are getting so good now that I wonder when that will no longer seem prudent. And with that said, my small camera takes such amazing (not studio quality) HD that I wonder when something like this would really seem like the best thing, especially considering they both take SD cards and length is only limited by SD card capacity.

It certainly does seem like a more professional camera in its size and shape, but mostly because that style has been the trend for some time now. But in a way this style is already starting to seem outdated, like a throwback. I also noticed, just now, that even the really big name manufacturers have this style in 1080p for comparable prices.

I'd definitely give this thing a look. I would have totally loved it a few years ago. The mic and extra lens still feel like premium features, but I'm rarely the one to set up for photos and video footage, as I usually just do landscapes or great spontaneous moments. This may be a fantastic alternative to giving kids your phone - or a phone - to play with. Seems like a good way to encourage their inner photographer without it leading into a bunch of cheap phone games.

Camera has mini* USB and HDMI ports (as opposed to micro) - just when I was wondering what I'd ever do with this one mini-HDMI cable I have... Mic takes 2xCR2032 batteries, which are included, and should probably last, as I don't think mics eat up much power. Has a curled, springy, analogue audio cable with stereo mini-plugs on both ends to connect the mic. Also has an external battery charger.
text_fidelity_b: HAOHUNT Camcorder Digital Video Camera HD 1080P 30fps 3.0 INCH Touch Screen 24MP Camcorder with Microphone and Wide Angle Lens Vlogging Camera with Remote Control Infrared Night Vision Recorder

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF-S 55-250mm F4-5.6 IS STM Lens with UV Protection Filter - 58 mm I purchased this lens on Amazon offered by a gray market vendor for $140 (new!). Gray Market means there is no USA Warranty. I haven't tried to see if it is eligible, but I assume it would not be. As of this writing (10/12/2014), that vendor, CD Supply, is still offering the lens - though now for $170. Still an incredible deal for this lens which came new in the standard Canon box with manual etc. (If it isn't warranteed - I can buy another and still be about the price of just one at regular price).

The lens itself: I was pleasantly surprised. I could have purchased it in my kit with the 70D camera, but wasn't really interested. For $140 - what the heck. The photos are sharper than from the kit 18-135mm STM IS lens in my opinion (and that's a pretty decent lens as kit lenses go). It is very small and light weight for a pretty long lens - especially on a crop sensor.
BONUS: Macro. It actually can get pretty decent magnification. Something like 1/4:1 from a pretty good distance at 250mm.
Plus it works great with extension tubes. I've used it with 12mm and 26mm (not together) and it worked great. Even autofocus - though I wouldn't recommend that for Macro.

Negatives (though - again - if you get it for cheap, these are quibbles):
- No lens hood provided. Buy a knock off on Amazon for $13
- Not a super bright lens. You're going to need some decent sunlight or a good flash with this. It ramps up to f/5 minimum pretty quick and f/5.6 not too long after that. Only the widest shots will get F/4.
- Pretty cheaply built (but it's a cheap lens!)
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 55-250mm F4-5.6 IS STM Lens with UV Protection Filter - 58 mm

Garmin 010-01985-01 Vivoactive 3 Music, Gps Smartwatch with Music Storage and Built-In Sports Apps, Black With all the options out for watches that double as smartwatches and fitness watches, I settled on this one for really 2 reasons. First, its from Garmin so you can expect that the GPS functions are going to be spot on. In that regard this watch is solid. The GPS is automatic as soon as you tell it that you are going to work out and it acquires quickly and its accurate. All you have to do is hit the single button on the side once, and select your activity. It usually locks in after about 10-15 seconds and off you go. This is critical for someone like me that pushes a stroller, steps never count right if you don't have GPS.

Second huge thing with this watch is the music function. I hate carrying my phone when i run and now, I don't! I set up spotify in a few minutes, downloaded 3 playlists (about 200 songs) and I'm good to go for my whole run. It makes it easy to hook to bluetooth and lets me either leave my phone behind when running or pull up a weight training app. The only drawback at all is that for the first about 2 minutes, it can have tiny skips if you are also running GPS, probably something to do with the watch not quite keeping up initially.

All in all this has been a great purchase and at a cost less than other options. We liked it so much, my wife got one too!

text_fidelity_a:
Munitio SV Mobile Performance Earphones with 3 Button Mic Control, Bronze Lower and mid end earphones have generally been lacking in both quality and performance. Given my propensity to misplace them, I have been reluctant to invest in more expensive versions. But with increased reliance on mobile devices, it was most definitely time to upgrade.

My familiarity with Munitio was more from their urban chic style complete with bullet motif, Kevlar coated cord, "tactical" carrying case and "hollow point" ear cups. At the risk of looking more Duck dynasty than cool, I was eager to try them.

Designed for use with Apple devices, the phones come securely packaged in a black carrying case. The look is sleek and modern and the bronze color is appealing. These are also available in black and gray. There are three sets of ear cups in different sizes. They were comfortable and shut out outside noise. The cord is flat and tangle free with a heft that promises durability. The 3 button mic control is located on the upper left hand side of the earphone cable. I really couldn't see the buttons but quickly mastered them by touch. They provide full functionality for calls and music on iPods, iPods and iPhones and just music for other mp3 players and Android devices.

I encountered no difficulties in making or taking calls. I could hear the other party and they could hear me without difficulty. The mic is positioned close enough to the mouth and is sufficiently sensitive that I didn't have to scream or repeat things. I made calls from a fairly busy coffee shop and a mall and ambient noise did not impair the call quality.

I tried these earphones with my IPod and a cheap mp3 player of dubious lineage. The sound was clear, strong and enjoyable. I did not find the bass overwhelming and was generally pleased with the performance.

Bottom line, I liked these earphones. The case and the trio of ear cups are thoughtful touches. Although light, there is a sense of substance and quality. The controls are intuitive and easy to use. There is a two year limited warranty. Serving up generous doses of comfort, convenience and performance, these ear phones are right on target.
text_fidelity_b: Munitio SV Mobile Performance Earphones with 3 Button Mic Control, Bronze

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2) I use earbuds a lot since I typically prefer the lightness and ease of use compared with traditional headphones. Right out of the box these were a bit puzzling as to how to position them for use. But, after a bit of fiddling with the over-the-ear loop, it becomes clear.

The in-ear comfort is good. It comes with a variety of ear tips including two types I’ve not used before: a double flange silicon tip and a triple flange silicon tip. The flanges allow the ear bud to make a much better seal in your ear canal. That not only helps cut out ambient noise intruding, it also improves the bass response. I found the double flange works best for me, but the variety of tips included appears sufficient to fit pretty much any ear.

It also comes with an excellent case for storage, and adapters for airplane use and for 1/4 inch plugs. I especially like the case since it’s small enough to make it easy to carry along (roughly 3.5 inches by 3 by 1.5 inches thick) and is reinforced to avoid being crushed. It has mesh pockets to keep everything stowed, and looks nice to boot (black with red contrast in the middle). All-in-all, it’s a great kit in terms of useful accessories.

I’m not as pleased with the cord. While I like how sturdy it is, it has a “Y” link that always seems to be in the way when I’m working out. I got used to it eventually, but a more streamlined cord system would have been a better design approach. Another negative is the 3.5mm plug. It needs to be seated just so or you get sound cut-outs or static. I tried it with several devices to be sure the issue is with the plug and not the device. A more robust plug is needed for this – you shouldn’t have to fiddle with it to get it to seat properly.

The over-the-ear loops are also a bit annoying at first. Granted, that’s certainly due to the fact that I usually use standard in-ear buds without the loop, so any type of loop feels weird to me at first. The material is soft and bendy, so you can position it in any variety of ways. It could benefit from some additional padding. On the plus side, they do hold the buds in very well. Quick head movements that would have loosened an in-ear bud didn’t jar these loose at all.

Now for the really important feature: how they sound. In a word, excellent. My benchmark for moderately-priced earbuds has been units made by RHA out of the UK. These sound nearly as good. Very clean sound but still ample bass provided that you select the right tip. For me, the standard tip (the one installed as delivered) gave me very little in terms of bass. Selecting a different tip to provide a better ear fit did wonders for bass response.

They are a bit more airy than the RHA sound. That could be a plus or a minus depending on your preferred type of music. Very heavy bass music is not a good match for these. Pretty much everything else is, and I appreciated the enhanced clarity. It’s the type of sound that, when you hear it, the first word that would come to mind is “clean.”

They look odd, make take you a moment to figure out how to position them, but provide a very open, natural sound. It comes with a well-designed kit of useful extras. However, the plug issues, the cord, and the ear loops collectively knock it down a star. Still well worth considering, however, and I would certainly recommend them.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)

Pixel Mago Canon Speedlite ETTL High Speed 5D2 5D3 6D 7D 60D External Speedlite While this flash doesn’t outperform the Canon Speedlite, it comes the closest of any of the Speedlite “clones” I’ve tried so far, and does so with impressive build quality.

I was impressed with this right out of the box mainly due to the care taken with packaging. No, packaging doesn’t impact the performance of the flash, but it does take the worry out of getting one that is damaged due to UPS handling. The flash is packed in a carry case (which is very well-made and has cushioning) and, in turn, packed inside of an air-filled tube case. Together they provide more than ample protection against transit-born bruises short of being run over by the UPS truck.

The flash feels very solid. The head articulates up/down/left/right and has indents at the most commonly used angles. The head is a bit stiff to move, but I consider that as a positive since I don’t want the head getting bumped out of place when I have it positioned the way I want it.

The hotshoe frame is plastic but feels very solid. There’s a rotating locking ring to keep it in place while on the camera. It made contact and worked just fine on a 5D Mark II, a 4D and a Rebel.

The battery compartment door has a spring-loaded hinge so it pops up when unlatched. Again, good build quality on that (which is a common point of failure on other low-cost flashes I’ve used). It uses 4 AA batteries. It ran fine on rechargeables.

The control panel and LCD screen are both easy to use and see for the most part. The buttons beep when pressed, but that can be turned off if you want a silent operation. Some of the icons on the screen are very small – I needed to squint a bit to make some of them out. Then again, my aging eyes could be a contributing factor.

Most of the commands are executed by pressing a button and then selecting options using a rotating wheel. The wheel is the only part that didn’t work all that well at times. Sometimes a single twist moved it through the menu; other times I needed to twist it a couple of times to get it to register.

The capabilities of this flash are very impressive given the price point. It offers synch flash, manual flash, curtain synch, up to 1/8000 second synch, master/slave mode, AF assist beam, TTL flash, zoom settings and an LED lamp. It also has a nice amount of convenience features such as auto off (with various timed settings ranging from 5 minutes to 2 hours), a lock mode, screen on/off and test mode. It even has a USB port that can be used to update the firmware should updates be available (at this writing I am not aware of any updates).

The manual is not great. It offers a decent listing of the capabilities, but is often sparse in pointing out the details. But, if you have some measure of experience with a flash, it’s not hard to figure out (with a bit of experimenting) how to use it.

Given the price, this is an excellent value. It probably won’t suit the needs of a professional photographer but for an amateur (even a very avid one) it’s an excellent alternative to Canon gear at a much nicer price.
text_fidelity_b: Pixel Mago Canon Speedlite ETTL High Speed 5D2 5D3 6D 7D 60D External Speedlite

Between that, the higher cost, and a few other things, I'm in the market for a different tablet and computer.

In the past, the problem switching back was that, unlike with Apple, things were not quite as user friendly with the interface and you had to really figure things out instead of it being immediately apparent.

Happily, it was different with this tablet. Out of the box, my family and I were able to figure it out quickly and easily, giving us hope in another option.

User-friendly layout, very accessible, good features, and it works seamlessly with Google. I've got google email and YouTube channels, so it's nice to know there's a trade-off for losing some of the other things like seamless transitions between iTunes, my current calendar (not in love with that--I can just as easily switch to google or droid for this)...

All this adds up to the following: Apple can no longer claim to be the clear leader in tablets, phones, and computers. They have stopped innovating far beyond comparable products, and now, for the value and overall performance, the ZenPad is a worthy adversary.

I still have my MacBook Pro computer, but when it comes time to buy a new one, I will be ready to switch knowing items like these are available.
What a great surprise!

text_fidelity_a:
Soundcore Upgraded, Anker Liberty Neo True Wireless Earbuds, Pumping Bass, IPX7 Waterproof, Secure Fit, Bluetooth 5 Headphones, Stereo Calls, Noise Isolation, One Step Pairing, Sports, Work Out I've used a few other true wireless headphones in the $50 price range (mostly unknown brands) as well as some more expensive brand name models (B&O, Plantronics). This set is better than most headphones in the under $50 price range. Sound is clear and noise free. Volume is loud enough for earbuds, but not booming at full volume. Bass is kind of weak, though that is a common problem in this price range. 3 hour battery life is about average for this price range. Comparing $50 headphones to $100 headphones is not really fair, but if you do want to spend more money, most headphones will give you much better bass and richer overall sound quality. More expensive headphones also give me better battery life (usually at least 4 hours without any recharging). On the other hand, if I'm out running or riding on the subway, I'd rather use these $50 headphones instead of risk losing much more expensive headphones.

I am impressed by the build quality of these Soundcore headphones. They headphones feel solid. They are comfortable in my ears. The case is sleek and the recharging system works well. The buttons that control the headphones work easily and reliably. I do wish they used a modern USB-C charging system instead of the old-fashioned micro-USB.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore Upgraded, Anker Liberty Neo True Wireless Earbuds, Pumping Bass, IPX7 Waterproof, Secure Fit, Bluetooth 5 Headphones, Stereo Calls, Noise Isolation, One Step Pairing, Sports, Work Out

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging I've been using both, and the main difference in usability is that the beanbag mount has a lower initial stability and higher reserve stability than the fold-flat mount.
In other words, the fold-flat will stay put better - until it breaks free, when it becomes completely free with no holding power. The beanbag is a little easier to get to shift on a bounce, but then it has enough mass to settle stably in its new position.
On the whole I prefer the beanbag as I'd rather have my GPS move around a little bit more than have it stay put better but then fly around uncontrolled.
Other differences are that the fold-flat mount is lighter and folds up smaller, much better suited to stowing away or traveling.
The fold-flat also lets the GPS vibrate more, the beanbag dampens vibrations, but this can be overcome by pushing the GPS down in the fold-flat mount until it stays in contact with the base.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging

Logitech Ultimate Ears 600vi Noise-Isolating Headset - Dark Silver These are amazing. They will fit. My ears are tiny. Most ear buds hurt after a while. With the smallest adapter in, these fit fine. The adapters cover a wide range of sizes, so you do need to test them all and find the best size for your ears. They work in two "modes" and I'm not sure they're supposed to. If you just sort of seat them in your ears, they act like normal earbuds (good for when you need some awareness of your surroundings). If you insert them the way you would ear plugs they act like noise cancelling earbuds (good for when you don't want to listen to the lady on the bus explain the ins and outs of her new baby's diaper). It just depends on how you sit them in your ears.

The sound quality excellent. I needed to turn down most of my devices because these transmit at a good volume--awesome if you like your music loud. The volume can be controlled on the cord. The microphone works nicely--I used mine with a Droid and the sound quality was fine. You can pause your MP3 player by pushing the button on the cord. Perfect for listening to podcasts and audiobooks.

They come with a carry case, which I thought a bit much for headphones, but I think I'll be using it. These are very good headphones, worthy of such care, and I want them to last a long time.

text_fidelity_a:
LG Electronics 70UK6570 70-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2018 Model) I bought this set for 4k gaming (PS4 PRO) and 4k films. Anything else like voice integration with google assistant was just a bonus that adds to the overall purchases and very happy with it.

The 70/75 inch model the only major difference is screen panel type. 75 is direct lit and 70 is edge lit. Features pretty much the same.

Out of the box the image using home mode was basic due the fact that all 4k TVs are set to automatic light detection and shifts the image to 'energy saver' slightly dimming them. Just go into the menu settings, picture setting and shut energy saving mode off. This is how all major tvs are shipped inbox. Its not a defect item. After shutting that off, the image settings work like normal. Vivid, sports, cinema etc they also have a professional tv set up for light and dark room. In case you want to hire someone professionally.

HDR effect is simulated HDR on SD content. Also a separate setting for HDR called: HDMI DEEP COLOR in 'additional picture settings' same location. They also have an option for eye strain, if its set on, shut it off. Its used for people who have eye strain from bright sets. I would keep HDMI DEEP COLOR ON to test that your HDMI is working with the TV, it will automatically turn on when it detects a blue-ray disk player with HDR or gaming system using it. Leaving it on, lets you know if the HDMI is compatible with it. Even if you're not using something with HDR. If the HDMI cant pass the signal, it will default to black screen 'no image detected'. In that case shut it off, and get a new HDMI.

After shutting off power saving modes, the tv works perfectly. Vivid images, sharp, major detail and awesome color. Whites are super white, but wont bleed over each other. Reds are blood red and blacks are dark. Everything pops off the screen, keep in mind i'm coming from a 1rst gen 4k tv that lacked a full HDR panel (10 bit). Slow remote response and lacking features that this set has. THIS new set fixes all that.. The blue tooth remote is responsive, fast and almost no lag, feel snappy and responsive. You can also download the LG app and use it as a pointer (like a mouse pointer on a computer). Easiest way to input information like passwords, email etc vs dialing them in on the remote. It can also be used as a pointer to navigate menu settings on screen with click being enter command.

LG has an app store, but haven't had a chance to play around with it. They give out free screensavers images in 4k, fireplace, beach etc and some basic games. In the future, i'll download wallpapers since my gaming is done on the PS4. They also have free apps for TV viewing from online channels. The set comes pre installed with Hulu, Netflix (controller has Netflix button), YouTube, google pictures etc you can also download free online shows that stream for free. From what I read online, Netflix is tuned to the TV for best viewing.

The set also has an update feature for firmware (under about TV settings sections) and you can set it to auto update. Once registered with LG, can also be done from TV. It allows you to use Google Assistance with a few prompts for basic set up. To fully use LG AI thinQ voice built in, you have to get a magic remote (under $50 bucks) and will be buying one soon, since I use voice features a lot. From google assistant from your phone, you can do basics, volume up +5, shut living room TV off and a few other commands that go threw google assistant (phone or google home) . The magic remote uses more the voice feature and you dont have to say: okay google, tell LG to turn off living room TV" saves you a step and allows you to use it for suggestions and what you see in the demo videos. Remember that AI ThinQ is working with Google assistant for results. Not a gimped voice feature like first generation 4k TVs.

My games look phenomenal, brand new including 4k films. Everything seems to have gotten a new coat of paint. The HDR really makes a difference in films and games. These set use HDR10 and HLG (Hybrid log gamma). The only thing it does not do is Dolby Vision. Its a Dolby version of HDR basically. Which to me isn't a deal breaker since HDR10 is more supported in films, streams etc

TV also supports fast wireless connection (wireless AC).

I have nothing negative to say about the set. Had an HDMI/HDR error and that was due to my HDMI not being high speed aka 'premium HDMI'. If you run into a similar issue with PS4 PRO, XBOX X or Blu-ray player. Connect directly to set should fix the issue and see if its the HDMI. Sometimes, like in my case, its an older HDMI that I had going from my sound system out to the LG TV. The PS4 was high speed/premium but the 2nd connection to the TV wasn't, so the chain was broken. Supported 4k but lacked bandwidth with 4k+ HDR.

This set has all major functions
VA panel
Wide Color Gamut (WCG)
4K Ultra HD Resolution
4K Active HDR
Ultra Luminance

UPDATE: 9/10/2018

Installed a new HDMI high speed cable from sound system out to TV from receiver and it fixed the 'no signal' sign when HDR was turned on. Leave HDMI DEEP COLOR ON. (it will pop up the logo) to let you know its working and not a black screen. if you get a black screen somethings wrong with the HDMI. When HDR is working and pops up the logo, go to settings (gear icons in remote), pulls up quick menu and HDR will be highlighted, but say HDR+Standard imaging viewing etc (can be changed). If you're using vivid (my personal choice) when using HDR, set it to HDR+ Vivid. When you do this again, and the TV detects an HDR signal again, it will remember the last HDR+(picture setting) mode you used. (HDR on or OFF) each has thier own image settings.

Random info: if you have a sound system connected to the TV, when using built in TV set apps (You-tube/Hulu etc) you may have to set the receiver/sound system to TV on its remote to get audio coming from the sound system. If you use a Blu-ray players apps, or apps from a game system like PS4 Hulu etc just setting the normal connection input should push the sound like normal.
text_fidelity_b: LG Electronics 70UK6570 70-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2018 Model)

Winegard HD8200U Platinum VHF/UHF HDTV Antenna (65 Miles+, Digital, 4K Ultra High-Def Ready) First, be aware this beast is more than 14 feet long and about 9 feet wide when unfolded and assembled. It does move in the wind. It doesn't weigh that much, but with so many elements forming such a large device it becomes a sail.

I mounted it on a 10' length of 1-1/4" electrical conduit held to a tall garage wall using [[ASIN:B001RCMEEA Channel Master CM-9025 3-Inch Heavy-Duty Wall Mount for TV Antenna Masts]]. The antenna is about 23 feet in the air.

The HD8200U has a very high-gain, directional Yagi UHF antenna on the front and a full VHF antenna on the rear. I really don't think I need the VHF section and may retire this antenna and opt for a more compact UHF Yagi if the high winds we occasionally experience cause trouble. After assembly, the two sections feed into an electronics box using 1/8" aluminum rods from each section. You then mechanically attach a top plate to the box that connects to all four aluminum leads. The coax connector is in this top plate. A weather boot is supplied to seal the connection.

The HD8200U does bring in the signal like a champ. My stations are at least 19 miles and 68 miles away. It's very directional. If I aimed 30 degrees off, I got zero channels. Check where your stations are broadcast from using www.antennaweb.org (antennaweb dot org) which provides distance and direction in degrees from magnetic north using your zip code. Very handy.
text_fidelity_b: Winegard HD8200U Platinum VHF/UHF HDTV Antenna (65 Miles+, Digital, 4K Ultra High-Def Ready)

The sound quality is fine, especially for small speakers. I don't expect them to rattle my windows are pump the base. The lack of a strong bass is noticeable (as mentioned, not a surprise) but I wouldn't call them tinny at all. The sound was quite pleasing and handled high volume with no distortion.

They're small enough to pack or easily move around or outside. They do connect to each other, with detracts from their convenience a bit, and I personally wouldn't have minded a longer connecting cable so as to spread the sound a bit farther apart, but since they're really not made for room-filling sound--aimed more at desktop or otherwise small spaces, it's hard to call that a major complaint or oversight. I prefer the Creative ZiiSound D3X to these--it's bit more convenient in that it's a single speaker set up and I thought its sound quality a little better, plus it has the ability to add in the subwoofer and other speakers (I have the subwoofer), but really, the difference isn't huge and the intent is somewhat different for most, so these speakers more than suit the bill for their size and purpose.

Logitech HD Laptop Webcam C615 with Fold-and-Go Design, 360-Degree Swivel, 1080p Camera I was able to compare this directly to the Logitech C525. They both have the same "fold and go" design, but I was surprised that the C615 is a bit heavier, and I think a millimeter or two thicker. It's well worth it, because the optics are better, and not just better because the resolution is higher - the quality is simply better.

The tripod mount is a nice addition over the C525, adding versitility in positioning. I suppose this would also help you set it up as a hidden camera, or just keep a pile of dirty laundry out of the view mounting on your laptop might otherwise provide.

As others have mentioned, there is a USB extender, which is nice. However, I would much rather have seen a long (or even a very short) cable provided with a microUSB connection to the actual device, allowing the device to become truly portable, rather than having a nice foldable, portable device with a cumbersome cord permanently attached. The user could then use the same cable they charge their smartphone with. Thankfully, the cord is placed in such a way that allows for full 360 degree rotation.

Note that although you can record 1080 videos with this device, you can only chat in 720 - another consideration if you just want this for Skype or another chat program.

Overall, this is the most appealing webcam on the market to me. The most important thing is that it can be tossed in a bag or pocket with other electronics without having to worry about the lens getting scratched.

bmanl Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth Headphones 48hrs Play Back Sport Earphones with LED Display Over-Ear Buds with Earhooks Built-in Mic Headset for Workout Purple BMANI-VEAT00L I purchased these to replace the Mpow Flame light that I had lost one of the earbuds too. I have gone through a couple of these.

What I do like is the charging case. It is pretty slim, it is USB C, and it also has a display to show how much of a charge it has. This is super helpful. It also has volume and connect/disconnect buttons. This has not yet had any charging issues, but I have not owned it for very long.

Now for what I don't like- They do not fit my ear that well. It may be the shape of hook, the length of the arm from which the speaker is mounted, or some other variable. The hook keeps it in place, but it never feels as if it's in my ear properly. I also think the sound is not so hot, and for 50 dollars I was expecting more. It is a little treble heavy on the heavier frequencies and just sounds like a cheap driver.

My previous headphone was the MPow Flame Lite. The charging case is bulkier and bare and there is no digital display. With that said- these are now 1/3 of the price. What I do like is that they fit my ear like a glove, and the sound quality is phenominal. It sounds like a much bigger driver. I am not an audiophile, but it really sounds great. Maybe it is the mid that come in fuller giving it a rich sound.

I have had some charging issues. Sometimes I find that only one of the headphones are dead and the other is fully charged. However, fit and sound are my most important details so these are my favorite. For the price I can purchase three and keep them in different places. If I lose one or have a charging issue I can replace it with the extra. This makes much more sense than keeping the aI do not more.

Edit: I changed from 3 to 5 stars. I have owned these now for almost one year, and use them probably every day. There has been no decrease in performance or battery life. I was so accustomed to my previous ear buds that I did not like these much at first. However, the sound is balanced, the battery life is great, and I really like the charging case. I have never actually times the batter life, but it is probably about 7-8 hours on a full charge. There are sooo many choices now for bluetooth ear buds, but these are a safe bet and most people should be happy. I am however not an audiophile, and someone who truly is may want to spend more on a Bose, or whatever the best ear buds are nowadays. My previous ones were more bass heavy, but these are better balanced. They do stay in the ear, unless I go to lay down on my back; I then have to push them back into my ear.

text_fidelity_a:
G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling I've had the opportunity to review three different G.G. Martinsen players, and of the three this one is my favorite. I brought two of the players, pre-charged, to review at my sister's where I am staying a week while she had and recovers from surgery, and the one thing I can say right off the bat is that I wish the charging cable was of the ubiquitous Micro-A type and not the mini type, which I did not think to bring with me. The [[ASIN:B016F4AGLC other player]] handles like the [[ASIN:B0173CW2CQ first one]] I reviewed for G.G. Martinsen, but I will have to wait until I get back home to do anything other than test the recorder and FM radio on this 16GB player because I have no cable to copy music onto the player with!

Anyway, unlike the other two players, the controls on this one make sense and handle more like what I'm used to. The instructions that come with this (that I also left at home!) were well-written in English, unlike so many products coming out of China these days. But I haven't needed the instructions to figure out how to use this player or change the settings. The first thing I did was set the Power Off and Sleep settings to 0 so the player won't shut off unless I flip the manual switch to turn it off. I have been listening to this player while I've been writing reviews, and I have had absolutely no cutouts with the FM radio even though I'm in a condo sandwiched on all sides by other units and this place is bad with reception of cable TV and other radios. I like that the station stays selected even when you power the player off and on again.

The control dial is easy to see, with a top Menu button, left and right arrows, and a pause/play button on the bottom (something the other players did not have). The round button in the middle has a good tactile feel, and even in the dark it's fairly easy to feel where to press for the different functions. I'll have to re-read the instructions to understand fully when to use the center button and how.

The little piece you can thread a lanyard into is plastic, but I don't think it will break easily unless you put a lot of stress on it. The player comes with a pair of original Apple-style earphones, which are great for walking outside where you need to be able to hear sounds around you while listening to music. The headphones are not the best in the world, but they are a nice additional feature and good to have in situations where you wouldn't want pricier headphones to get ruined (the gym, outside should it start raining). Of course, your listening experience will only be as good as the wired headphones you plug into this player. It really is a whole lot of bang for the buck and an attractive little player. I have the turquoise color, and it's really nice.

I put links to the other two players I have reviewed so you can compare them. What I like about this one is it doesn't have that gimmicky bubble-gum type selection screen but, rather, just has a list of the different features and functions. The list is easy to read and looks more businesslike and professional than the more cartoonish screens of the other two players.
text_fidelity_b: G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz S5 IEM Noise Isolating Earphones with Clearwavz Remote and Microphone for iPhone iPad iPod I’m a big fan of the Brainwavz S1 (actually all of their headphones – have yet to be disappointed with any of their products). The S1 has been my main set for active use (e.g., workouts, runs, etc.) since the flat cable is very durable and resistant to tangles. The S5 keeps all the good features of the S1 and adds to it – the sound quality is richer and better defined.

That’s not to say the S1 sounds poor – they are quite good, in fact. But the S5 are better. The highs are better defined and the midrange has more punch to it. The bass comes through clearly without moving into the harsh territory when the volume is pushed (as the S1s can do). The overall sound quality is very pleasing.

The build quality seems solid – as solid as the S1 or better. I love the flat cable! I know that’s something that is not appreciated by everyone, but for me it’s been working out wonderfully. Although this (as most other Brainwavz headsets) comes with an excellent hard shell case, I usually tote my earbuds wrapped around my mp3 player in my pocket. Easy to carry; very stressful on the cables and can lead to tangles with round wires. Flat wires, especially those with a thick jacket such as these, survive that abuse with zero problems.

The earbuds themselves are more sleekly shaped than the “can” style of the S1.

Comfort is in line with the customary Brainwavz style, which is to say it’s outstanding. It comes with a wide range of tips to fit pretty much any ear, plus the Comply foam tips (which are my favorite). If fitted properly you end up with zero ear irritation plus excellent sound isolation and bass response.

These are an over-the-ear design much like the S1. I never used that design prior to the S1 and it did take me a little time to get accustomed to it. It became second nature quickly, and the design is a lot more stable when exercising than the conventional in-ear design.

These are more expensive than the S1, but you can hear the difference in price. Still, if you’re looking to keep the cost down a bit, the S1 is an excellent performer as well.

Great sound, great comfort, wonderful cable design, and it comes with a solidly made case and lots of eartips. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz S5 IEM Noise Isolating Earphones with Clearwavz Remote and Microphone for iPhone iPad iPod

I want to write the review here so that other shoppers won't make a mistake.  The manufacturer might have a good idea but the product is worse than a toy.  If I could give a zero star, it would make a zero or a minus star.

HP Wireless Elite Keyboard v2 ...if you don't have a wrist rest or pad already, I highly recommend that you get one at the same time you get this keyboard. I was introduced to the chiclet- or scissor-style keyboard because of using one at work (using an Apple wired keyboard with an Intel Mac), and I have to say that I prefer it in every way to the more traditional keyboards. It is much quieter, and, for me, the feedback is pleasant. One thing I did not take into account, though, is that I had a wrist rest at work. So when I got this keyboard for home use and started using it, I loved it immediately--until the day I used it for hours on end. Then--ouch! My wrists began to ache.

Overall, this is a great keyboard. It connected to my computer without a problem, and the only lag in keystrokes I have experienced has been when the computer had just been "awakened" from sleep mode. For reasons I will not go into here, I am using this keyboard with a laptop: the laptop keyboard's lights indicate whether or not I have Caps Lock or Num Lock engaged on the wireless keyboard. I understand that won't help people using this keyboard with a desktop computer, but thought I'd put it out there anyway.

My conclusion: if you're a fan of the scissor-style keyboard and you have or are willing to invest in a wrist rest, you will enjoy this keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: HP Wireless Elite Keyboard v2

Polk Audio RC65i 2-way Premium In-Wall 6.5" Speakers, Pair of 2 Perfect for Damp and Humid Indoor/Outdoor Placement - Bath, Kitchen, Covered Porches (White, Paintable-Grille) I was really impressed with how easy these were to install. The user's guide clearly walked me through the process even though these were the first in-wall speakers I've installed. It also comes with a very handy template to ensure it's a "cut once" process with no regrets (or spackle). Since there's a lip on the frame you don't need to be worried about making a perfectly smooth cut through the drywall since the rough edges are hidden.

I was torn between these and the RC80i model. Both had identical tech specs on the Polk site. What sealed the deal in terms of the RC85i model is that it is a bit more shallow than the RC80i (depth of 2 and 7/8 inches for the RC85i versus 3 and 1/4 inches with the RC80i). More importantly, the tweeter assembly on the RC85i is a bit different. According to Polk, the tweeter in the 85i has a plate underneath it that helps project the sound. This is not found in the 80i.

But the proof is in the sound, and these sound wonderful. I'm using them in a basement wired to a Denon AV receiver in the LR. While the sound can't compete with the Kef's I have in the LR, the Polks sound far better than I expected given the price. Very pleased!

They also are very aesthetically pleasing. The grill is nicely made, and can be painted. As with installation, clear and detailed instructions on painting the grills are in the user's guide.

Good sound, good looks and good price - can't ask for more! Highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White I've had my two Echo Dots for one year now. Now, a year later, Google Home has really come forward by leaps and bounds while Alexa has basically stayed exactly the same. For Android users, the easiest way to describe it is that the Alexa has become an iPhone vs. Google's Android. I think I am the norm in that there is almost no "Skill" I have use for with Alexa. Instead I ask things that are already built in features: weather, time, set alarm, add things to shopping list, and of course, control home devices like lights. However, ALL home devices can do those things just as easily and intuitively as Alexa does, so to see if you are getting the best device you need to compare other features:

Asking a question - Google wins hands down. Google uses... Google, to get your answer. Alexa uses Bing I think, nuff said. Most of the time the response from my Dot is "I'm sorry, I don't know that" and if it does "know", it is giving an answer to something I'm not truly asking. For example, I asked it what movies were playing on FOX tonight and the response was "I'm still learning about fox. Ask me a fox fact so I can learn more about them." Many times it even just answers to search the internet. Well, if I have to search the internet then I want to use Google to do it and there is no way to set your search engine. Essentially every time it tells me to search the internet, what I hear in my mind is "Use Google" - yeah, I think I just might, Amazon.

"Skills" apps - all but useless for every day life. Skills I can see some possibility of using are the reading a bedtime story if you have kids, or asking Alexa to play a game. But for adult life and for truly being a life/home assistant to you, none of the Skills compare at all to the platform that Google already has in place from decades of being an internet powerhouse. Example: finding your phone. This is a pretty common issue that I think it's reasonable to assume any of these home assist devices should be able to tackle easily. For Alexa you must download a "Skill" (there are a few to choose from) and register your phone number to that app. The major flaws with Alexa doing this are: 1. you need to first tell Alexa to open and use the skill with precise wording for it to work (i.e. "Alexa find my phone" won't work. "Alexa have Tracker find my phone" won't work. "Alexa open the Tracker app. Alexa have Tracker find my phone" won't work. "Alexa open the Tracker app. Alexa ask the Tracker app to find my phone" works). 2. if your ringer is off there is no ability to turn it on for the purpose of finding the phone. Essentially you'd be better off to add "me" to contacts with your own number and just tell Alexa "call me" because that is all you are getting with Alexa's "Skills", it's easier to just do that, and it only has the same flaw of not ringing if ringer is off. In comparison, with Google you download nothing, simply say "Google find my phone", and viola, your phone will ring whether the ringer is on or not. Google also has "Maps" which is huge. "Maps" gives you locations, hours of operation, can list like-businesses, tell you how to get somewhere and how long it will take you, and even tell you which buses to take if you have public transit in your area, etc. Alexa can only utilize Yelp and if a business isn't on Yelp then Alexa has no access to even the very basic info Yelp supplies (hours).

There's one 'Pro' to Echo over any other home device, and that is as it relates to other Amazon devices. Like Google, Amazon is also an internet powerhouse in it's own way. Having a Prime membership is the norm rather than the exception in most households, and obviously that means asking Echo to order something or play a Prime movie or Prime music is going to be smooth and easy with the Echo. Also, where Amazon still leads the pack is with it's Fire Stick, and again, obviously, Echo is going to be well integrated with that device, while other Home Assistants aren't given that level of access to integrate as well. So that's why I give it 2 stars - because I can't use my FireStick AS EASILY if I owned something other than an Echo. But I can still use the remote so that ability is def not worth more than two stars, especially when Google has the ability to take away access to things like YouTube (which it did) from Amazon in retaliation for being denied access to things like FireStick integration into it's own device.

Bottom line, Echo/Alexa seems great until you see how much better the later competitors to the market have improved on the user experience and are continuing to improve by leaps and bounds with each new update, while Amazon rests on 'we were the first'. Or, in other words, don't fall for yet another same ol' iPhone that is introducing features Android users have had for at least five years when instead you could just buy the Android and have the newest and best features right now.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

AMD FD8350FRHKBOX FX-8350 FX-Series 8-Core Black Edition Processor Immediately after installing I noticed the idle speed just sitting in BIOS to be 50C. That's quite a bit! More than any processor I've come across.
At first I thought I seated it wrong so I undid the heat sink, used really good thermal paste and tried once more.
Same result. Idle temp at 50C.
And under load it's getting up to into the low 60s and termal throttling like crazy. However it seems to perform well even under that heavy load, which is nice if that's all you care about.
But I'm doing a build for my dad and I don't think he'd be content with having to hear a jet engine under his desk day in and day out. So I'm going to have to look elsewhere.
That's on me though. I probably should have known better from my experience with another FX processor. Ah well.
Still considering if I'm returning this or not.

UPDATE:
Ok, I did some more digging and it sounds like my motherboard is not equipped to handle this processor.
WARNING: If you have a MSI 970A-G46 Motherboard DO NOT BUY THIS PROCESSOR.
Go research "MSI 970A-G46 FX 8350"
You'll find numerous testimonials of people who have had terminal issues trying to use a FX 8350 with this board.
Since the MB is at fault for this and I can not accurately benchmark this product, I'll give AMD the benefit of the doubt and make this 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: AMD FD8350FRHKBOX FX-8350 FX-Series 8-Core Black Edition Processor

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Wireless Reading Device (6" Display, U.S. Wireless) I am probably one of the least intuitive people around when it comes to technology. I've bought quite a few gadgets that have ended up collecting dust as I never really learned to use them properly. My short lived relationship with a Palm Pilot ended in frustration when I didn't learn how to back it up on my PC and all my carefully inputted data was lost (more than once!) My kids use it now for a doodle pad. My husband says I have a "black thumb" when it comes to anything electronic. If there is a way to break it, lose it, or misuse it, I'm right there doing it. This is why it is so astonishing that I have grown to love my kindle 2.

I learned how to use it easily within a few minutes. It is so intuitive- my four year old enjoys it and can page back and forth reading classics such as George MacDonald's The Princess and The Goblin or Mary Pope Osborne's The Magic Treehouse. My tween age son uses it for Shakespeare- I downloaded the First Folio (35 plays from the Bard) for all of 99 cents! It's quite a favorite amongst my children and I have recently learned that if more than one family member has a kindle, all e-books may be shared with a single purchase. My friend can even access her kindle books and magazines from her iphone!

Cool features include 6 different options for font size, and text markers by "location" to bring you to the same line of text whether you use the biggest or smallest of fonts, as page numbers would vary too much to be useful. A male or female voice can read to you, though the voices are a bit stiff and robotic, and they make small mistakes such as using alternate pronunciation that don't fit context with heteronyms such as read/read or live/live. You can connect speakers or earbuds/headphones for this feature. Magazines can be downloaded as a single issue or a subscription, but the subscriptions cannot be canceled from the kindle- the user must go to amazon's "Manage my kindle" area to do this.

I have downloaded quite a few classic books for free and spent about a dollar on many others. So far, the younger children's literature has been somewhat limited, but I imagine that as prices drop, more will become available. I am a bibliophile and I never thought I would love a paper book replacement, but this device is so clean and glare free that I forget I am not looking at a paper page.

I'm sure that color kindles will be available within a few years, to make the illustrations a bit more interesting. I love the beautiful pen and ink type renderings which fill the kindle 2 screen when it isn't in use. Obviously though, color would be more attractive with other types of art. Black and white is easiest on the eyes for text, and mostly that it what kindle is all about.

The kindle 2 holds a charge for a long time. I think I plug mine in about once every couple of weeks. If you are not careful with the five way button, sometimes you do end up getting the wrong result. text_fidelity_a:
LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports Disclaimer: I was sent this product to evaluate so that I could write an informed review.

Actually this is my second LotFancy cooling pad, and I took it because I do like their products. I haven't had any bad experiences with them except for breaking off one of the little plastic stops that keeps your laptop from sliding off the pad when the rear is elevated, but that was entirely my fault. I left the pad on the floor and someone stepped on it. Can't blame LotFancy for that.

The design of this pad is kind of interesting. It has two controls, one for the large center fan and the other for the four smaller side fans. This, plus the width of the pad itself, allows you to use various sizes of laptop efficiently. If you have a small one, you never need to turn on the side fans. If you have a 17" one, they're in position to help you cool it. I'm curious as to why the green light (signaling that the center fan is on) is set so much lower than the light for the side banks. A strange feature, though not something I have a problem with. It's just odd.

The pad is adjustable to seven different heights (including flat), so you've got a lot of positions to choose from. I write in a variety of places around the house, so this is one of my favorite things about the pad. It allows me to work without having to find all sorts of things to prop my laptop on. The locking mechanism is solid. Since it's USB-powered, there's an extra USB port at the back so that you don't lose that functionality. Most cooling pads have some way of doing this, so it's expected rather than special. It's quiet, but it's far from super silent.

It's a good pad. Yes, some of the construction seems a bit flimsy, but my other LotFancy pad has held together just fine and I see no reason to think this one won't.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports

text_fidelity_a:
XSories Big U-Shot Monochrome Monopod Telescoping Camera Pole 3 Feet Extension (Atlantic Blue) This is a step up from a regular monopod in that it telescopes down to a belt-hangable tool. In full extension, it's the right height to use when, say, sitting watching a performance at an event, allowing you to stabilize a phone or camera for recording comfortably. The head at the top pivots and locks into position. I like that the larger end also has a standard screw fixture that can take either the carbiner clip or be fitted to a standard tripod, which gives this a lot of flexibility. A monopod tends to be easier to move around with than a tripod.

The telescoping portions each individually lock. Getting them to lock into position so they don't slip is a little fiddly; it takes getting a feel for twisting one way or the other to loosen or tigthen and also being sure to tighten enough so it doesn't loosen on its own. On the whole, though, this is a very useful little tool. We plan to use it with our freestanding desktop camcorder to record poetry readings we're involved with so we can put them online as well as to hold our digital camera when we're out and about.
text_fidelity_b: XSories Big U-Shot Monochrome Monopod Telescoping Camera Pole 3 Feet Extension (Atlantic Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
Nikon D5000 12.3 MP DX Digital SLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6G VR Lens and 2.7-inch Vari-angle LCD My D5000 was delivered yesterday evening while I was at work. The lovely wife opened the box enough to pull the battery out and charge it for me. After a grueling 12 hour shift at work I had forgotten about my new toy.

I had purchased the D5000 w/ 18/55 kit lens then separately purchased a 55/200 VR kit lens. It was cheaper that way. Go figure.

After many doggie slobbers when I arrived home I noticed the D5000 box on the kitchen table. My heart started palpating. I tried to control my self to no avail. My new toy was here! I carefully unpacked everything. I actually followed the quick start guide and was ready in no time.

I'm a big guy with the requisite big hands. The D5000 felt good in my hands. Not too heavy, not too light. The black body was finished with a slightly rough tactile coating. Very nice. My right thumb fit nicely in the thumb spot while my right index finger felt at home on the shutter. With a firm grip on the D5000 I was able to fully articulate my wrist and point the camera in a variety of positions. The camera felt good in my hand. I could tell that I could lug this beauty around for a full day and not get the dreaded "photog's wrist syndrome."

I attached the 18/55 kit lens. The lens seemed to provide a better balance when attached to the body. The VR switch, on the lens, was factory set to OFF. My first few images didn't utilize the VR. I was so excited and getting more excited by the minute that I forgot the properly look at the lens. I could notice the difference between the VR switching. This 18/55 kit lens is quite amazing. Sure it's made out of plastic, but it does a great job. If you don't already have Nikon lenses then the 18/55 kit lens is a no brainer. Well worth it.
As the quick guide said...Frame your first subject...then BAM!

I was looking for subjects to shoot. Since I work nights everyone, except the dog, was asleep. So I can't run around flipping light switches, move knick-knacks, or anything that could involve waking the baby. God forbid I wake the baby. My wife would have my testicles drawn and quartered within 7.9 seconds. Of course it's been raining for 2 days straight. So I'm stuck in the house...with a new camera. No worries!

I really like the D5000. Coming from the "superzoom point & shoot world" this is a welcome, although a little scary, change. I used film SLR cameras up until the late 90's so I have some experience with SLR photography. But the digital advances sure make everything so much easier. I'm not a "all manual all the time" kind of guy. Like most of us, I want the added feature of full-manual to play with, but like having an excellent and fast AUTO feature. I like to spend time with my family when we're all out and about and don't like to fiddle with any settings. The family gives me plenty of time, on my own, to experiment.

I added some images above.
text_fidelity_b: Nikon D5000 12.3 MP DX Digital SLR Camera with 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6G VR Lens and 2.7-inch Vari-angle LCD

I then connected the first unit to my PC through the USB port and the touchscreen began working afterward. The same cure worked on the second unit. Software glitch I thought.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony FDRAX53/B 4K HD Video Recording Camcorder (Black) An astonishing example of technology like nothing I've ever seen before.

It's been forty years (!) since I first saw a video camera in high school, a big b/w camera with a backpack that contained the batteries and internals. It was impressive! Then we used a kind of mini-VHS video recorder to share kid videos with our parents maybe 15-20 years ago. Then I got an iPhone which had kind-of video capabilities. So I guess I was ripe to be blown away by this Sony FRAX53/B.

It's small and compact, like a small football. The swing-out screen is breathtakingly crisp and the internal operating system and menus are not only in color, but accompanied by clear, bright sound! I charged the battery and took a video of one of my cats. I could not believe the clarity of the image when I viewed it on the screen! The video is of such high quality that it's easy to overlook the still camera, which is remarkable. High-resolution, bright images. The "Photo" button is kind of oddly placed, it's not easy to operate it while you're holding the device with its right-side hand strap. You can also use a "Manual" mode and twist the lens to achieve custom focus. There's a 20X optical magnification which ought to satisfy anyone.

The Sony software is thorough and functional. The camcorder will transfer photos and video wirelessly if you have a fairly modern computer. I had to use a PC laptop rather than my elderly Mac. That meant using Windows 10, which led to some baffling moments trying to figure out if anything was working.

Between the Sony software and the camcorder and our WiFi setup and Windows 10 I found that the best thing to do sometimes was just WAIT. Windows would give me bad information and I would misinterpret that as an error. Ignore what Windows is telling you and be patient while the FDRAX53/B does its work.

The printed manual is basic and you'll want to spend time reviewing the online documentation. I'm still trying to figure out how to use the Sony FDRAX53/B and a "U-Stream" service to get a live stream going. There is a LOT of technology packed into this camcorder! Expect to spend some time reviewing it all. As I mentioned, Sony packed a TON of features in this device, and there's a learning curve to really understand and appreciate them all.

If you're planning a vacation or expecting a newborn child, BUY THIS CAMCORDER! You cannot take enough videos and photos of your kids when they're young, and the same goes for vacations -- this camcorder is small enough to tote with you (it does not like fog or water, though!) and the QUALITY of the images are incredible! It's not so heavy that it's going to be a burden.

The sound is very good, and there's a "gun" style microphone if you want to A) avoid wind noise B) capture audio of what you're shooting (like at a kid's soccer game) rather than local chitchat.

One thing that occurred to me while I was fiddling with the camcorder in my right hand, that being that if you were holding one of your kids in your left hand and the camcorder in your right hand and they both began to slip... which would you grab? This camcorder is THAT nice. Between the quality of the camcorder and its fantastic lens and the Sony software for image management and manipulation, this could be a major hobby in and of itself. You can easily edit, trim and combine videos with sound and add captions and text. For a consumer level product, the video and image editing suite is quite impressive. You will want a fairly modern computer, as I mentioned.

Something I come back to again and again as I figure the FDRAX53/B out is the absolute wonder of it. The small size, the quality of images, the ease of operation -- I just can't get over it. Beyond sensational and well into the realm of magical. I've never seen anything like the FDRAX53/B before.
text_fidelity_b: Sony FDRAX53/B 4K HD Video Recording Camcorder (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG 23.5” CF396 Curved Computer Monitor, AMD FreeSync for Advanced Gaming, 4ms Response Time, Wide Viewing Angle, Ultra Slim Design, LC24F396FHNXZA, Black Now, in all fairness, I probably just spoiled myself rotten when I bought a $5000.00 Eizo professional monitor 8 or 10 years ago. Prior to that I'd been using two much less-expensive Samsung monitors and had been perfectly happy with them (excepting their longevity - neither of them lasted more than two or three years before going completely dead). Then, as I was embarking on a career as a pro photographer, I decided I needed a professional-quality monitor with precise and consistent color reproduction, so after hemming and hawing over the price for a while, I bit the proverbial bullet and laid down the cash for a new Eizo ColorEdge CG276. And honestly, at that time, I noticed that what I saw on my screen looked very nice, but I don't recall it blowing my mind - proof that the way to *really* appreciate what you've got is to do without it. Because I've now tried replacing this Eizo monitor (which is still working perfectly in every respect and which I'm still using and writing this review on now) with less expensive monitors twice, and each time I've shaken my head in disbelief that anybody could use a monitor with such crappy resolution and image quality, let alone think it was good.

That, sadly, but I guess as is to be expected, was my experience with this Samsung.

It didn't matter that the screen was curved; what I saw on the screen looked so terrible that it wouldn't matter if the monitor was a freaking planetarium, or a perfect globe surrounding me on all sides while I floated in the center via...I don't know...jetpack or something. I'd just have that much more poorly rendered graphics to look at.

I've attached five photos: one of the progress bar as it appears on my Eizo monitor, and two as it appears on this Samsung, followed by one of the Apple logo as it appears on the Eizo and finally, the Apple logo as it appears on the Samsung. You be the judge. (UPDATE: I just noticed that Amazon's website doesn't display the images in the same order in which you upload them (or at least it isn't with my images)...so suffice it to say that the really smooth and nice-looking progress bar and text and Apple logo are the Eizo's screen, and the really jaggy, glary, awful-looking ones are the Samsung's.)

I don't have the technical understanding of monitors required to explain which monitor-related variable it is, exactly, that makes the image quality on this Samsung so unsatisfactory (resolution? pixel size/shape? dunno.), but something definitely does it.

Maybe once you've used an Eizo on a Mac, you can never go back. So be it. If I really need a new monitor I'll just save my pennies until I can afford another Eizo...or at least something with much better specs than this Samsung. Because boy, was it a disappointment.

Ah well...lesson learned (kinda...even though I don't really know *why* I thought the Samsung sucked). I've boxed it back up and arranged my hassle-free return through Amazon and will at least get my money back...the return policy and process being two reasons I buy through Amazon in the first place. And I'll simply content myself to go on using a top-quality flat screen (that I can smoothly and easily raise and lower and pivot and even turn from landscape to portrait and back!) instead of trying to swap it out for a vastly inferior curved one (that I can only tilt up and down).
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 23.5” CF396 Curved Computer Monitor, AMD FreeSync for Advanced Gaming, 4ms Response Time, Wide Viewing Angle, Ultra Slim Design, LC24F396FHNXZA, Black

I called them and they said that when this happens, "...unplug the Fire TV for 15 seconds and then plug it back in." In my opinion, that takes the fun out of watching a movie! I thought the memory and quad-core processor would be enough to stop this from happening, wrong! Having said that, instead of naming my review "ROKU on Steroids" I should have named it "Just like ROKU".

The Amazon rep said that it was a problem with the memory of the Amazon Fire TV and not the video. When asked if the problem could be fixed by Amazon with an update, all he said was "I'll forward that to Amazon".

If you don't mind watching videos that stop playing and having to unplug the Fire TV and restart it during a movie, you'll really like the Fire TV.

One other point, the Amazon rep stated that it might be my router. I have an Apple Airport Extreme, the best and fastest available. If it was my router, I guess the Amazon rep should have had me unplug my router instead of the Fire TV. He finally admitted that it was the Fire TV and not the router.

Just wanted to get this information out there so people can be informed about the Amazon Fire TV before purchasing one. All in all, I'm happy with the Fire TV...just aggravated that I have to unplug it and restart it when watching movies. The Amazon Fire TV should be better than this!
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation
